- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or mean of last 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (0.3–0.7), model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average if deviation >3%.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model tends to underestimate price peaks in bullish sentiment cycles; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment >0.6 over last 7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop; forecast should be 1–2% lower than model to reflect stronger downward momentum.
